clue.text: Sophisticated, so it's said, after spells here, perhaps?

definitions.text: Sophisticated, so it's said, after spells here, perhaps?

indicators.note: places the sophisticated word behind the spells

parts.note: charms are magic spells; the final S of 'charms' runs into the next word when spoken

indicators.note: signals that the words are spoken rather than spelt, so their sound is what goes into the grid

parts.note: cool is informal for sophisticated; with the S of 'charms' run on, it is said as 's-cool'

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a place teaches people to become sophisticated by casting spells on them.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, 'charms cool' runs together into the answer. The whole clue also defines it: a place you might go to come out polished.
explanation.definitionFit: A charm school is an establishment teaching poise and etiquette, exactly where one would learn polished manners.

clue.text: Check on a violent disturbance in carriage

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check
a riot is a violent public disturbance

explanation.surface: Someone is told to keep an eye on an outbreak of trouble inside a carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A chariot is a two-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle of antiquity, a kind of carriage.

clue.text: Irritate some? Small number inside

indicators.note: tells us one piece goes within the other here

parts.note: any can mean some, as in 'have you any?'
NO is the abbreviation of number (No.), a short form of it

explanation.surface: Does it irritate anyone when only a handful of people are indoors?
explanation.definitionFit: To annoy someone is to irritate or bother them, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Marvel? Marcel, I suspect

indicators.note: as an adjective suspect means dubious or not genuine, so the letters are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: Is it a marvel? Marcel is doubtful, says the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I suspect' reads as the speaker's hunch; the I is fodder and 'suspect' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A miracle is a wonder or astonishing event, the sense of a marvel.

clue.text: Far too much silver in church residence

indicators.note: places the other pieces inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
OTT is 'over the top', meaning excessive
AG is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A church residence holds an excessive amount of silverware.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottage is a small house, a modest kind of dwelling or residence.

clue.text: Key worker in action

definitions.meaning: the ... word is the key one
an ... law or system is in force and working

explanation.surface: An essential employee is busy on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key worker' looks like one phrase (an essential employee) but splits into two separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Operative means crucial, as in 'the operative word', also a worker, and also functioning or in effect.

clue.text: Backache caused by taking piano out of plant

indicators.note: with 'out of', taking something out of a word means deleting it
with 'taking', names the word the letter is removed from

parts.note: plumbago is a flowering plant, also called leadwort
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A gardener blames their bad back on hauling a piano out of the shrubbery.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbago is pain in the muscles of the lower back.

clue.text: Riddle has to be missing second shoe

indicators.note: tells us a letter is lacking from the word

parts.note: a riddle is a coarse sieve, a strainer

explanation.surface: A puzzle seems to be about a lost second shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddle' looks like a puzzle but is the sieve sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer is the British name for a sports shoe or sneaker.

clue.text: Met geisha, slyly, at college? You've been found out!

indicators.note: doing something slyly is doing it deviously, so the letters are cunningly rearranged

parts.note: UP means in residence at university, as in 'up at Oxford'

explanation.surface: Someone who sneakily met a geisha while away at university is told they've been rumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: 'The game is up' is an idiom telling someone their deception has been discovered.

clue.text: Flask carried by brother, mostly

indicators.note: the answer is borne within the following words, spanning their letters

explanation.surface: A flask is mostly carried around by someone's brother.
explanation.definitionFit: A Thermos is a vacuum flask, from the trademark name.

clue.text: Chocolate cake made by caterers, tho' badly

indicators.note: done badly, the letters come out in a muddled order

explanation.surface: A chocolate cake was made by caterers, though poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: Sachertorte is a rich Viennese chocolate cake with apricot jam.

clue.text: Girl I married over in cathedral city

indicators.note: places the turned piece inside the city

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

indicators.note: in a down-or-across clue, over means turned back to front

explanation.surface: A girl tells of marrying in a cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns IM into MI, which goes inside ELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Emily is a female first name, so an example of a girl.

clue.text: Cleaner, by a stop, caught early coach

parts.note: a char is a charwoman, a cleaner
to ban is to stop or forbid
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A cleaner waiting at a stop catches a coach early in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'early' belongs to the definition: a charabanc is an old type of coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A charabanc was an open motor coach of the early twentieth century, used for outings.

clue.text: Item, extremely large, at rear of lorry

indicators.note: puts the extremes after the lorry

parts.note: an artic is an articulated lorry

indicators.note: takes the extremes, the outermost letters, of the next word

explanation.surface: A very large item sits at the back of a truck.
explanation.definitionFit: An article is a single object or thing, an item.

clue.text: Old country house table in good condition

parts.note: a chart is a table of data
well means healthy

explanation.surface: An old country house has a table still in good shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartwell in Kent was Winston Churchill's country home, a historic manor.

clue.text: Record one's poem for part of series

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
one is I as a Roman numeral, so one's becomes I'S
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: Someone records their own poem for an instalment of a programme.
explanation.definitionFit: An episode is one instalment in a broadcast serial.

clue.text: Clarify former patent

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
patent as an adjective means obvious, plain

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to make clear the terms of an earlier patent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patent' looks like the noun for an invention licence; it is the adjective meaning obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: To explain something is to make it clear, i.e. clarify.

clue.text: Saw wanderer entering empty pub

indicators.note: signals one piece going inside another
an emptied word keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: a rover is someone who roams

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a drifter walking into a deserted pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' reads as the verb but is the noun for an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim, as is a proverb.

clue.text: Husband leaving kitchen having been cooked English kipper?

indicators.note: cooked means falsified or reworked, so the letters are scrambled
a letter leaving a word is removed from it

explanation.surface: A husband leaves the kitchen once his English kipper has been cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' drops H from KITCHEN, and 'having been cooked' rearranges KITCEN into NECKTI. A kipper is also a wide, garish 1960s-70s tie.
explanation.definitionFit: A kipper tie is a very broad necktie, so a kipper is one example; the question mark signals this.

clue.text: Appropriate gathering bound for shabby cinema

indicators.note: one piece gathers the other, i.e. holds it within

parts.note: fit means suitable, appropriate
a bound is a leap

explanation.surface: A suitable assembly is headed for a run-down picture house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathering' looks like a noun meaning a crowd, and 'bound for' like a destination; 'gathering' is the containment signal and 'bound' a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleapit is a jocular British term for a dingy, run-down cinema.

clue.text: Fine offer resolved it

indicators.note: something resolved is broken down and reformed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A good offer settled the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' rearranges OFFER into FORFE; 'Fine' reads as approval but is the noun for a penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: A forfeit is a penalty paid for a wrongdoing, as a fine is.

clue.text: Log remark that's humiliating

definitions.meaning: to record it in writing, as one logs it

explanation.surface: Write down a demeaning comment.
explanation.definitionFit: To put down is to record in writing; a put-down is a snub or humiliating remark.

clue.text: Proudly display evidence of accident in fast vehicle

parts.note: to sport something is to wear or show it off
a scar is the mark left by an injury

explanation.surface: Someone shows off the battle damage on their speedy car.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports car is a fast, low-built automobile designed for performance.

clue.text: Stumble heading off to change

indicators.note: with its heading, its first letter, taken away

parts.note: to falter is to stumble

explanation.surface: A trip on the way out prompts a change of plan.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter is to modify or make different.

clue.text: Name appearing in parish theatre

indicators.note: one piece shows up inside the other

parts.note: a parish is a local area

explanation.surface: A name is showing at the local playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a place of action or contest, as in 'theatre of war'.

clue.text: Quietly feel offended by award

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction to play quietly
to resent is to feel aggrieved at

explanation.surface: Someone is privately aggrieved at a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'award' is the verb: to present a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: To present is to bestow or give something formally, as one awards a prize.

clue.text: Grotesque building I recognised in broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means put on air, so the phrase is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: to recognise is to have seen, so I recognised is I saw

explanation.surface: Someone spotted an ugly structure on a TV programme.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech, 'I saw' and the answer sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is something ugly to look at, often an unsightly building.

clue.text: Get round by coach, express

parts.note: a round is a single bullet or cartridge
to coach is to train

explanation.surface: Someone is told to go about by coach, quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'express' reads as the verb or adjective, but it's the noun for a fast train.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullet train is a high-speed passenger train, such as Japan's Shinkansen, a type of express.
